blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.prompt: Meet me at the hotel bar.
exercises.why: **встретиться → Встретимся** — perfective verb, 1st person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Let's all pitch in and get the work done.
exercises.why: **подналечь → подналяжем** — perfective verb, 1st person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future. Давай — one person (ты); Давайте — several people, or one person by вы; the verb is the same.

exercises.q: Я лишь надеюсь, что дождь ___ (повременить) ещё пару часов.
exercises.prompt: I only hope that the rain holds off for a few hours more.
exercises.why: **повременить → повременит** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: We will sign it for you.
exercises.why: **расписаться → распишемся** — perfective verb, 1st person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.q: Теперь ___ (приступить) к детальному изучению кода в нашей обычной манере.
exercises.prompt: Now we’ll examine the code in detail, in our customary fashion.
exercises.why: **приступить → приступим** — perfective verb, 1st person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.q: Когда я пукну, и сановники начнут смеяться надо мной, ___ (обнажить) мечи.
exercises.prompt: When I fart and the dignitaries begin laughing at me, draw your swords.
exercises.why: **обнажить → обнажите** — perfective verb, 2nd person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.q: Столбы ___ (отстоять) друг от друга на три метра.
exercises.prompt: The posts are spaced three meters apart.
exercises.why: **отстоять → отстоят** — present-type form, 3rd person plural: ending -ят belongs to the second (и) conjugation.

exercises.prompt: I hope the fog will go away soon.
exercises.why: **рассеяться → рассеется** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: These flowers are just about to bloom.
exercises.why: **расцвести → расцветут** — perfective verb, 3rd person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: That'll teach you!
exercises.why: **научить → научит** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Let's stop at the next gas station.
exercises.why: **остановиться → остановимся** — perfective verb, 1st person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future. Давай — one person (ты); Давайте — several people, or one person by вы; the verb is the same.

exercises.q: Если Джейсон мне ___ (позвонить), скажи ему, что меня нет.
exercises.prompt: If Jason calls me, tell him I'm not here.
exercises.why: **позвонить → позвонит** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Can you clean the mess up?
exercises.why: **разобраться → разберёшься** — perfective verb, 2nd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Tom will be an adult soon.
exercises.why: **повзрослеть → повзрослеет** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: This medicine will ease your cramps.
exercises.why: **облегчить → облегчит** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Tom is a conspiracy nut.
exercises.why: **двинуть → двинут** — perfective verb, 3rd person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.q: Если все ___ (внести) свою лепту, у нас получится.
exercises.prompt: If everyone pitches in, we can do it.
exercises.why: **внести → внесут** — perfective verb, 3rd person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Tom doesn't have long to live.
exercises.why: **прожить → проживёт** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: We'll meet you downstairs.
exercises.why: **встретить → встретим** — perfective verb, 1st person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: I'll deal with Tom later.
exercises.why: **заняться → займусь** — perfective verb, 1st person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.
